newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends firm on fund buying, CBOT support.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends firm on fund buying, CBOT support.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended higher and well above their earlier lows on short covering by commission houses and spillover support from CBOT grains and soybeans, traders said.

"I don't think you can really point to anything fundamental," a trader said. "We had another wave of commission-house buying at the close. Beans rallied off their lows. Volumes were very active within the last half-hour."
Wheat staggered at the open, driven lower by technical selling tied to Tuesday's close. But the selling dried up and wheat climbed off its lows by the midsession.
KCBT wheat ended four to six cents per bushel higher, with Sept up four cents at $4.49 per bushel. Dec also gained four cents to close at $4.32-1/2.

Refco topped the players' sheet, having bought 2.5 million Dec bushels, traders said. FIMAT and Wolcott & Lincoln each bought 1.3 million March bushels. Continental bought one million Dec. General Mills and Shay Grain each sold one million Dec, sources said.
KCBT estimated Wednesday's wheat futures volume at 32.605 million bushels, down from 34.00 million on Tuesday.
